hypotheses.statement: The database connection pool exhaustion was caused by increasing worker concurrency from 8 to 32 without increasing the pool size from 20, creating contention for limited database connections
The token expiry caused settlement failures because the settlement-worker fails closed when it cannot read the settlement_v2_enabled flag from flags.internal
The combined failure ratio of approximately 0.69 (0.38 + 0.31) matches the observed peak failure ratio of 0.61, with some overlap where both faults affected the same attempts
The concurrency change and token expiry occurring within four minutes of each other suggests a possible common root cause in deployment or configuration management processes

observed_facts.statement: The settlement-worker concurrency was increased from 8 to 32 workers at 15:55:00Z without adjusting the database connection pool size of 20
Database connection pool exhaustion occurred at 15:58:10Z with pool size 20, checked-out 20, causing pool_timeout errors affecting approximately 0.38 of settlement attempts
The feature-flag service token expired at 15:59:00Z after a 90-day validity period that began on 2025-11-13
Calls to flags.internal returned 401 invalid_token from 15:59:02Z, causing settlement-worker to fail closed when unable to read settlement_v2_enabled flag, affecting approximately 0.31 of attempts
Settlement failure ratio reached 0.61 at 16:00:44Z against an objective of 0.02
Increasing the connection pool to 64 at 17:20:15Z eliminated pool_timeout errors and reduced the failure ratio from 0.61 to 0.29
Installing a replacement token at 18:12:10Z eliminated 401 responses and reduced the failure ratio from 0.29 to 0.004
The two faults (pool exhaustion and token expiry) started four minutes apart and neither explains the other
The incident ticket INC-2201 recorded no settlement value at risk

open_questions.missing_evidence: Configuration management documentation or design decisions explaining the relationship between worker concurrency and connection pool sizing
open_questions.question: Why is the database connection pool size not derived from or automatically adjusted with worker concurrency changes?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Inventory of service tokens with their issuance dates, validity periods, and renewal automation status
open_questions.question: Which other service tokens are on manual renewal schedules and may be at risk of similar expiry-related failures?

open_questions.missing_evidence: Financial impact assessment or settlement value metrics for the incident duration
open_questions.question: What was the actual settlement value at risk during the incident, and why was this not recorded in the incident ticket?

summary: Payment settlement failures occurred due to two independent faults: (1) database connection pool exhaustion caused by increasing worker concurrency without adjusting pool size, and (2) feature-flag service token expiry causing authentication failures. The faults started four minutes apart and collectively caused a peak failure ratio of 61% against a 2% objective. Remediation occurred in two steps: pool enlargement resolved pool exhaustion (reducing failures to 29%), and token replacement resolved authentication failures (reducing failures to 0.4%).

timeline.statement: Settlement-worker concurrency increased from 8 to 32 workers without adjusting the database connection pool size of 20
Database connection pool exhausted with pool size 20, checked-out 20, queue depth rising, causing pool_timeout errors affecting approximately 0.38 of settlement attempts
Feature-flag service token expired after 90-day validity period issued on 2025-11-13
Calls to flags.internal returning 401 invalid_token, causing settlement-worker to fail closed when unable to read settlement_v2_enabled flag, affecting approximately 0.31 of attempts
Alert fired: settlement attempts failing reached 0.61 against objective of 0.02
INC-2201 opened with severity 1, title 'Settlements failing', recording no settlement value at risk
Connection pool raised to 64, pool_timeout errors stopped, settlement failure ratio fell from 0.61 to 0.29
Responder noted pool_timeout errors gone but questioned why 29% of settlements still failing
Responder identified two separate faults: pool exhaustion from concurrency change at 15:55 and token expiry at 15:59
Replacement token for flags.internal installed, 401 responses stopped, settlement failure ratio fell from 0.29 to 0.004
Responder noted both faults fixed but raised questions about why pool size is not derived from worker concurrency and which other service tokens are on manual renewal
